original_value: With limited resources, it is quite challenging for cloud providers to meet dynamic and massive customers' demands. Higher utilisation or refusing any service level agreement (SLA) may lead to penalties which play a crucial role in the cloud business. Overutilisation of resources, instead of maximizing the revenue, may lead to a decrease in revenue due to the SLA violations. Various studies have been conducted to investigate these issues; however, there is still room for improvement. In this study, the authors proposed a model to address the resource scalability and SLA violation issues by hiring external resources at low prices. However, in contrast to a federated cloud, the proposed model allows a provider to hire resources from any external provider with flexible terms and price. They designed algorithms to optimise providers' revenue by taking into account different parameters, including resource utilization, customer satisfaction, SLA violation, and prices. Simulation result shows that the proposed model is efficient in handling massive demands, and improves revenue generation and customer satisfaction. Offering joint pricing on customers' choice and outsourcing the extra workload to external resources leads to revenue maximization. Hiring external resources earns external revenue as well as it maximizes the total revenue.

result.paraphrase: With limited resources, cloud providers find it difficult to satisfy dynamic and large customer demand. Raising utilisation or declining any service level agreement (SLA) can trigger penalties, which are vital in the cloud business. Rather than increasing revenue, resource overutilisation can reduce it because of SLA violations. Although many studies have examined these problems, there is still scope for improvement. In this study, the authors proposed a model to address resource scalability and SLA violation issues by hiring external resources at low prices. Unlike a federated cloud, this model lets a provider obtain resources from any external provider under flexible terms and pricing. They developed algorithms to maximise provider revenue while considering factors such as resource utilization, customer satisfaction, SLA violations, and prices. Simulation results indicate that the proposed model efficiently handles massive demand and improves both revenue generation and customer satisfaction. Joint pricing based on customers' choice and outsourcing excess workload to external resources leads to revenue maximization. Hiring external resources brings in external revenue and also maximizes total revenue.
